quality_note: NISAR data are provisional. Calibration and validation are carried out by the NISAR project (NASA-JPL and ISRO), not by our team. This series MIXES provisional products with pre-calibration BETA products (dates before 2026-06-17); treat amplitudes before that date with extra caution.

equivalents.millerton_lake_source: USBR Friant Dam / Millerton Lake (~520,500 acre-ft = 0.642 km3)

literature_comparison.relevance: Establishes that inelastic aquitard compaction volume equals permanent groundwater storage capacity loss.

literature_comparison.source: Smith et al. (2017), Water Resources Research (Southern San Joaquin Valley 2007-2010)
literature_comparison.relevance: InSAR-derived permanent storage loss of 0.414-0.748 km3 over 3 years (~0.138-0.249 km3/yr annualized).

literature_comparison.source: Ojha et al. (2018), Scientific Reports (San Joaquin Valley 2012-2015 drought)
literature_comparison.relevance: 0.4%-3.25% permanent storage-capacity reduction alongside ~24-29 km3 total groundwater depletion.

method: Permanent aquifer storage loss V_loss = sum((-v_permanent_vertical) * A_pixel) integrated across valid decomposed pixels (reason == 0, within Central Valley bbox, active threshold v_vert < -1.0 cm/yr; net all-valid integral also reported). Line-of-sight permanent rates from 25-pair harmonic-linear fit (2025-11-24 to 2026-10-14) are projected to vertical via pixel-wise incidence angles (cos theta, median 41.5 deg). Uncertainty combines 1-km block-correlated standard error (13x13 px) with empirical 3-reference sensitivity re-referencing.
assumptions: Assumes inelastic compaction dominates the linear permanent trend term (v_cm_per_yr), while seasonal elastic recovery is absorbed by the annual sin/cos terms.
Vertical projection assumes predominantly vertical compaction (v_vert = v_los / cos(theta)), neglecting minor horizontal tectonic/lateral motion.
Series mixes 18 pre-calibration beta pairs (before 2026-06-17) with 7 provisional pairs (quality='mixed'); pre-calibration amplitudes carry extra uncertainty.
Only valid coherent pixels (46.0% of bbox) are integrated; decorrelated irrigated fields inside the bowl are not extrapolated, making the integrated volume conservative where coherence drops.
Standard errors of cumulative InSAR epochs are temporally correlated; 1-km block aggregation reduces but does not eliminate spatial/temporal correlation.
